record.original_question: It is known that there exist residually finite, locally finite, characteristically simple groups with finitely many orbits under automorphisms(A. B. Apps, J. Algebra, 81(1983), 320–339). Are there any locally finite, characteristically simple groups with finitely many orbits under automorphisms that are not residually finite?

evidence.quote: It is known that there exist residually finite, locally finite, characteristically simple groups with finitely many orbits under automorphisms(A. B. Apps, J. Algebra, 81(1983), 320–339). Are there any locally finite, characteristically simple groups with finitely many orbits under automorphisms that are not residually finite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called locally finite if every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is finite. It is called characteristically simple if it has no proper nontrivial subgroup that is invariant under every automorphism of $G$. It is called residually finite if for every nonidentity element $g \in G$ there exists a normal subgroup $N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$. The automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ acts on $G$ by $g \mapsto \varphi(g)$; the orbits of this action are called the automorphism orbits of $G$, and one says $G$ has finitely many orbits under automorphisms if this action has only finitely many orbits.

It is known that there exist residually finite, locally finite, characteristically simple groups having only finitely many orbits under automorphisms.

Question: Does there exist a locally finite, characteristically simple group with only finitely many orbits under automorphisms that is not residually finite?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search of the Kourovka Notebook and related literature did not yield a confirmed resolution of this question. Related work exists on soluble groups with few automorphism orbits, and Apps's 1983 construction provides residually finite examples, but no published source located in the search confirms whether a non-residually-finite example exists or has been ruled out.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies groups G with finitely many Aut(G)-orbits, focusing on soluble groups of finite rank.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research addresses related orbit-finiteness questions but not this specific characteristically simple, non-residually-finite case.
